```ts
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { Platform } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { AccountExport } from "../../auth";
import type { ModerationExport } from "../../moderation";
import type { ProfileExport } from "../../social";
import { AccountError, type AccountDeps } from "../context";
import type { OpenFile, ZipWriter } from "../zip";

/** One export a day (1b design, section 10). */
export const EXPORTS_PER_WINDOW = 1;
export const EXPORT_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

const exportLimitKey = (userId: string) => `export:${userId}`;

/** The entry an image has in the archive; export.json names it under the post's media. */
export function mediaEntry(id: string): string {
  return `media/${id}.webp`;
}

/** The download's name: the handle and the day, so several exports of one account sort by date. */
export function exportFilename(handle: string, now: Date): string {
  return `korbat-export-${handle}-${now.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}.zip`;
}

/**
 * What the archive is written from. The account's own facts, the profile and the moderation member are
 * read before the first byte; the profile's lists are read page by page while export.json is written,
 * and the images, each behind the media module's checked open, go first, so `missingMedia` is complete
 * by the time the JSON that lists it is written.
 */
export interface ExportPlan {
  exportedAt: Date;
  /** The handle of the session that asked for the export: the id the auth module lists each session under. */
  currentSession: string;
  account: AccountExport;
  profile: ProfileExport;
  /** The decisions about the account that it was told of and its own reports, as the moderation module hands them over (3c design, section 7.11). */
  moderation: ModerationExport;
  images: { id: string; open: OpenFile }[];
  /** The images whose file the checked open refused or could not find, filled while the images are written. */
  missingMedia: string[];
}

/**
 * Counts one export of the account in the daily window and refuses once it is used up. Taken before
 * anything is built or streamed, so a stream that fails midway still counts; Retry-After says when the
 * window resets.
 */
export async function enforceExportLimit(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string): Promise<void> {
  let hit: { count: number; resetMs: number };
  try {
    hit = await deps.limits.hit(exportLimitKey(userId), EXPORT_WINDOW_MS);
  } catch {
    // Fails closed: an export that cannot be counted is not made, and the client is told to retry shortly.
    throw new AccountError("service_unavailable", 503, undefined, 30);
  }
  if (hit.count > EXPORTS_PER_WINDOW) throw new AccountError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, Math.max(1, Math.ceil(hit.resetMs / 1000)));
}

/**
 * Gives the day's export back after a failure before the archive's first byte (a pool timeout, a
 * restart): the owner received nothing, so the attempt must not use up the day. Best effort: when the
 * store cannot be reached, the export stays counted and a warning says so, which costs the owner a day
 * at worst.
 */
export async function giveBackExport(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string, log: Logger): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await deps.limits.release(exportLimitKey(userId));
  } catch (err) {
    log.warn({ err, userId }, "account export: the day's export could not be given back after a failure before the first byte");
  }
}

const iso = (at: Date): string => at.toISOString();
const isoOrNull = (at: Date | null): string | null => (at ? at.toISOString() : null);

/** What an account module built without the moderation module writes: the member is part of the format, so it is always there. */
const NO_MODERATION: ModerationExport = { decisions: [], reports: [], strikes: [] };

/**
 * Reads what is needed before the first byte: the account's facts, sessions, devices and events (one
 * read, bounded by the 90 days of events), the profile's own fields, the list of images, and the
 * moderation member (the decisions the account was told of and its own reports, both short lists). The
 * four modules are asked at once, so a read that fails costs the owner nothing: no byte was sent yet.
 * `currentSession` is the handle of the session asking, which marks its entry among the sessions.
 * `pageSize` is how many rows of each profile list are read at a time; tests lower it.
 */
export async function buildExport(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string, currentSession: string, now: Date, pageSize?: number): Promise<ExportPlan> {
  const [account, profile, images, moderation] = await Promise.all([
    deps.auth.exportAccount(userId),
    deps.social.exportProfile(userId, pageSize),
    deps.media.exportImages(userId),
    // The server always hands the moderation module over; a test of the other members may leave it out.
    deps.moderation ? deps.moderation.exportFor(userId) : NO_MODERATION,
  ]);
  return { exportedAt: now, currentSession, account, profile, moderation, images, missingMedia: [] };
}

/** A list member of export.json, read in pages and written one element at a time. */
class Paged<T> {
  constructor(
    readonly pages: AsyncIterable<readonly T[]>,
    readonly element: (row: T) => unknown,
  ) {}
}

/** An array already in memory, as one page. */
function inMemory<T>(rows: readonly T[], element: (row: T) => unknown): Paged<T> {
  return new Paged(
    (async function* () {
      yield rows;
    })(),
    element,
  );
}

/** Fragments are gathered into pieces of about this many UTF-16 units, at most 3 bytes each in UTF-8: well under 64 KiB. */
const PIECE_CHARS = 16 * 1024;

/**
 * export.json in pieces, written exactly as JSON.stringify(document, null, 2) writes the whole
 * document: member by member at the top level, and the lists element by element, each element
 * stringified on its own and indented to its depth (JSON.stringify's output holds line breaks only
 * between tokens; one inside a string is escaped, so indenting after every line break is exact). No list
 * is ever whole in memory: each is read page by page as it is written.
 */
export async function* exportJson(plan: ExportPlan): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  let buffer = "";
  for await (const fragment of documentFragments(plan)) {
    buffer += fragment;
    if (buffer.length >= PIECE_CHARS) {
      yield buffer;
      buffer = "";
    }
  }
  if (buffer.length > 0) yield buffer;
}

async function* documentFragments(plan: ExportPlan): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  const { account, profile } = plan;
  const ref = (row: { postId: string; at: Date }) => ({ postId: row.postId, at: iso(row.at) });
  const other = (row: { handle: string; since: Date }) => ({ handle: row.handle, since: iso(row.since) });
  // The members in the order of the format (ExportFormat in the contracts); the order is part of the bytes.
  const members: [string, unknown][] = [
    ["format", "korbat-export-1"],
    ["exportedAt", iso(plan.exportedAt)],
    [
      "account",
      {
        id: account.account.id,
        email: account.account.email,
        createdAt: iso(account.account.createdAt),
        role: account.account.role,
        mfaEnabled: account.account.mfaEnabled,
        hasPassword: account.account.hasPassword,
        verified: account.account.verified,
        termsVersion: account.account.termsVersion,
        termsAcceptedAt: isoOrNull(account.account.termsAcceptedAt),
        // Inside the account, where the format places them; at most the cap of ten, so they are written with the account's other facts rather than paged.
        passkeys: account.passkeys.map((passkey) => ({ name: passkey.name, createdAt: iso(passkey.createdAt), lastUsedAt: isoOrNull(passkey.lastUsedAt), synced: passkey.synced, createdOn: passkey.createdOn })),
      },
    ],
    [
      "profile",
      {
        handle: profile.profile.handle,
        displayName: profile.profile.displayName,
        bio: profile.profile.bio,
        createdAt: iso(profile.profile.createdAt),
        handleHistory: [...profile.profile.handleHistory],
        // Last in the profile, where the format added it (2c); the member order is part of the bytes.
        showInExplore: profile.profile.showInExplore,
        // After it, where 3e added it (W.8): the retired handles of the history, with when.
        retiredHandles: profile.profile.retiredHandles.map((retired) => ({ handle: retired.handle, retiredAt: iso(retired.retiredAt) })),
      },
    ],
    [
      "posts",
      new Paged(profile.posts, (post) => ({
        id: post.id,
        body: post.body,
        createdAt: iso(post.createdAt),
        replyToId: post.replyToId,
        quoteOfId: post.quoteOfId,
        state: post.state,
        deletedAt: isoOrNull(post.deletedAt),
        media: post.media.map((image) => ({ id: image.id, file: mediaEntry(image.id), altText: image.altText, width: image.width, height: image.height })),
      })),
    ],
    ["likes", new Paged(profile.likes, ref)],
    ["reposts", new Paged(profile.reposts, ref)],
    ["bookmarks", new Paged(profile.bookmarks, ref)],
    ["following", new Paged(profile.following, other)],
    ["blocks", new Paged(profile.blocks, other)],
    ["mutes", new Paged(profile.mutes, other)],
    [
      "sessions",
      inMemory(account.sessions, (session) => ({ id: session.id, createdAt: iso(session.createdAt), lastUsedAt: iso(session.lastUsedAt), current: session.id === plan.currentSession })),
    ],
    [
      "devices",
      // The platform column is text; sign-in only ever writes one of the contract's three values.
      inMemory(account.devices, (device) => ({ label: device.label, platform: device.platform as Platform, firstSeenAt: iso(device.firstSeenAt), lastSeenAt: iso(device.lastSeenAt) })),
    ],
    ["events", inMemory(account.events, (event) => ({ type: event.type, at: iso(event.at) }))],
    // Complete by now: the images were written before the JSON.
    ["missingMedia", inMemory(plan.missingMedia, (id) => id)],
    // Last, where the format added it (3c). Each entry is written member by member in the format's order, so the bytes
    // do not depend on how the moderation module builds its objects, and nothing beyond the format is ever written.
    ["moderation", moderationMember(plan.moderation)],
  ];

  yield "{\n";
  for (const [index, [key, value]] of members.entries()) {
    yield `${index === 0 ? "" : ",\n"}  ${JSON.stringify(key)}: `;
    if (value instanceof Paged) yield* listFragments(value);
    else yield indented(JSON.stringify(value, null, 2), "  ");
  }
  yield "\n}";
}

/** The moderation member with every entry's members in the order of the format (ExportFormat in the contracts). */
function moderationMember(moderation: ModerationExport): ModerationExport {
  return {
    decisions: moderation.decisions.map((decision) => ({
      id: decision.id,
      decidedOn: decision.decidedOn,
      postId: decision.postId,
      kind: decision.kind,
      outcome: decision.outcome,
      ground: decision.ground,
      ruleId: decision.ruleId,
      rulesVersion: decision.rulesVersion,
      measures: decision.measures.map((measure) => ({ kind: measure.kind, mediaId: measure.mediaId, noEffect: measure.noEffect })),
      reversals: decision.reversals.map((reversal) => ({ kind: reversal.kind, mediaId: reversal.mediaId })),
      facts: decision.facts,
      reason: decision.reason,
      legalReference: decision.legalReference,
      appeal: decision.appeal === null ? null : decision.appeal.state === "pending" ? { state: "pending", result: null } : { state: "answered", result: decision.appeal.result },
    })),
    reports: moderation.reports.map((report) => ({
      ref: report.ref,
      receivedAt: report.receivedAt,
      ground: report.ground,
      ruleId: report.ruleId,
      category: report.category,
      explanation: report.explanation,
      items: report.items.map((item) => ({ position: item.position, link: item.link, reexamines: item.reexamines, outcome: item.outcome, outcomeText: item.outcomeText, reexaminationOpen: item.reexaminationOpen })),
    })),
    // 3e (W.8): the strikes the account was given.
    strikes: moderation.strikes.map((strike) => ({ decisionId: strike.decisionId, postId: strike.postId, ruleId: strike.ruleId, givenAt: strike.givenAt, countsUntil: strike.countsUntil, overruledAt: strike.overruledAt })),
  };
}

/** A top-level member's array, as JSON.stringify writes it at that depth: "[]" when empty, else one element per line group. */
async function* listFragments<T>(list: Paged<T>): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  let first = true;
  for await (const page of list.pages) {
    for (const row of page) {
      yield `${first ? "[\n" : ",\n"}    ${indented(JSON.stringify(list.element(row), null, 2), "    ")}`;
      first = false;
    }
  }
  yield first ? "[]" : "\n  ]";
}

const indented = (json: string, pad: string): string => json.replaceAll("\n", `\n${pad}`);

/**
 * Writes the archive: every image as a stored entry, then export.json, then the central directory.
 * export.json comes last so that missingMedia can name every image whose file the checked open refused
 * or did not find when its turn came (the sweeper may be between the row and the file), or that was no
 * longer the owner's to export by then: the media module reads each image's row again as it opens the
 * file, and opens none for an image deleted with its post, erased or sealed since the list was read.
 * The order of entries means nothing to a reader.
 */
export async function writeExport(writer: ZipWriter, plan: ExportPlan): Promise<void> {
  for (const image of plan.images) {
    if (!(await writer.addFile(mediaEntry(image.id), image.open))) plan.missingMedia.push(image.id);
  }
  await writer.addJsonPieces("export.json", exportJson(plan));
  await writer.end();
}
```

```ts
import type { AuthErrorCode, MeProfile, Profile, StaffErrorCode } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import type { Mailer } from "../mail/mailer";
import { decodeKey, parseVersionedKey, type VersionedKey } from "./crypto";
import type { KeyValueStore } from "./kv";
import type { Lockout } from "./lockout";
import type { BreachChecker } from "./passwords";
import type { AuthRepo } from "./repo";
import type { Sessions } from "./sessions";
import type { TurnstileVerifier } from "./turnstile";
import type { VerificationProvider } from "./verify/provider";

export interface AuthConfig {
  appOrigin: string;
  /** Origins allowed to send cookie-authenticated state-changing requests. */
  allowedOrigins: string[];
  authHmacKey: Buffer;
  ipHashKey: Buffer;
  totpKey: VersionedKey;
  /** Keys TOTP_ENC_KEY replaced; still accepted for decryption. */
  totpPreviousKeys: VersionedKey[];
  /** Encrypts a signed-out notifier's name, address and mail token (3c design, section 6.1); see NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY in config.ts. */
  notifierKey: VersionedKey;
  /** Keys NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY replaced; still accepted for decryption. A contact is never encrypted again under the new key. */
  notifierPreviousKeys: VersionedKey[];
  termsVersion: string;
  /** How the client address is read; see TRUST_PROXY in config.ts. */
  trustProxy: "cloudflare" | "caddy" | "none";
  /** Who checks the phone number behind the verified badge; see VERIFY_PROVIDER in config.ts. With `off` the badge routes answer badge_unavailable. */
  verifyProvider: "off" | "dev" | "vonage";
  /** The relying party passkeys are bound to; see WEBAUTHN_RP_ID and WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME in config.ts. */
  webauthn: {
    rpId: string;
    rpName: string;
    /** The origins a ceremony's clientDataJSON may name. */
    origins: string[];
  };
  /**
   * The staff console (3a design, section 8): the only origin a staff ceremony's clientDataJSON may name and the relying
   * party staff keys are bound to, CONSOLE_ORIGIN and CONSOLE_RP_ID. Null while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset: the console is
   * off and no staff route is mounted.
   */
  console: { origin: string; rpId: string } | null;
}

export function authConfigFrom(config: Config): AuthConfig {
  return {
    appOrigin: config.APP_ORIGIN,
    allowedOrigins: [config.APP_ORIGIN, ...config.TRUSTED_ORIGINS],
    authHmacKey: decodeKey(config.AUTH_HMAC_KEY),
    ipHashKey: decodeKey(config.IP_HASH_KEY),
    totpKey: parseVersionedKey(config.TOTP_ENC_KEY),
    totpPreviousKeys: config.TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS.map(parseVersionedKey),
    notifierKey: parseVersionedKey(config.NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY),
    notifierPreviousKeys: config.NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS.map(parseVersionedKey),
    termsVersion: config.TERMS_VERSION,
    trustProxy: config.TRUST_PROXY,
    verifyProvider: config.VERIFY_PROVIDER,
    webauthn: {
      rpId: config.WEBAUTHN_RP_ID,
      rpName: config.WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME,
      // A passkey ceremony run from a development origin (Expo's dev server, say) is accepted outside production only:
      // in production the web app is served from APP_ORIGIN, and no other origin may use its passkeys.
      origins: config.NODE_ENV === "production" ? [config.APP_ORIGIN] : [config.APP_ORIGIN, ...config.TRUSTED_ORIGINS],
    },
    // The configuration fills CONSOLE_RP_ID with the console's hostname whenever CONSOLE_ORIGIN is set.
    console: config.CONSOLE_ORIGIN === undefined ? null : { origin: config.CONSOLE_ORIGIN, rpId: config.CONSOLE_RP_ID! },
  };
}

/** Public profiles live in the public schema, which the auth module cannot reach; the API supplies this. */
export interface ProfileStore {
  /**
   * Writes the profile and the reservation of its handle. Refused with `handle_taken` when another profile holds or held the
   * handle, `handle_retired` when korbat retired it (3e), and `handle_reserved` when the database's guard of handles
   * refuses one of the placeholder's form that a caller let through.
   */
  create(input: { id: string; handle: string; displayName: string }): Promise<{ ok: true; profile: Profile } | { ok: false; reason: "handle_taken" | "handle_retired" | "handle_reserved" }>;
  /** The owner's view of their profile, which /me returns: the public facts plus the handle-change date, the badge and the Explore switch. */
  find(id: string): Promise<MeProfile | null>;
  /** Sets or clears the badge (profiles.verified_at), which the auth module decides but cannot write itself. */
  setVerified(id: string, at: Date | null): Promise<void>;
}

export interface AuthDeps {
  repo: AuthRepo;
  kv: KeyValueStore;
  sessions: Sessions;
  lockout: Lockout;
  mailer: Mailer;
  turnstile: TurnstileVerifier;
  breachChecker: BreachChecker;
  profiles: ProfileStore;
  /** The phone verification provider behind the badge, or null when VERIFY_PROVIDER is off. */
  verify: VerificationProvider | null;
  config: AuthConfig;
  log: Logger;
  now: () => Date;
}

/** Per-request facts the flows need. The IP is already hashed; the raw address never enters a flow. */
export interface RequestContext {
  ipHash: string;
  userAgent: string | undefined;
}

/** A staff request's facts: those of any request, and its id, which the audit rows it writes carry (3a design, section 6). */
export interface StaffRequestContext extends RequestContext {
  requestId: string;
}

export type AuthErrorStatus = 400 | 401 | 403 | 404 | 409 | 429 | 503;

/**
 * The auth codes, the staff console's (the module owns staff keys and sessions, and the staff routes raise its codes as
 * AuthErrors, 3a design section 10), plus the shared one the module also raises, as the social and media modules do: a
 * well-formed request that asks for nothing, such as the current address as the new one.
 */
export type AuthErrorKind = AuthErrorCode | StaffErrorCode | "invalid_request";

const MESSAGES: Record<AuthErrorKind, string> = {
  invalid_code: "That code is not valid. Check the latest email or request a new code.",
  code_expired: "That code has expired. Request a new one.",
  too_many_attempts: "Too many attempts. Request a new code.",

  password_check_unavailable: "We could not check that password right now. Try again in a moment.",
  staff_mfa_required: "Staff accounts must keep two-factor authentication on.",
  onboarding_required: "Choose a handle to finish setting up your account.",
  mail_unavailable: "We could not send the email. Try again in a moment.",
  rate_limited: "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.",
  handle_cooldown: "Handles can change once every 30 days.",
  email_in_use: "That email address already belongs to an account.",
  phone_in_use: "That phone number is already verified on another account.",
  badge_unavailable: "Verification is not available on this korbat.",
  verify_unavailable: "We could not reach the verification service. Try again in a moment.",
  passkey_invalid: "That passkey did not work. Try again or use your email.",
  passkey_unsupported: "This passkey provider is not supported. Try another one.",
  // The cap of 10; the flow passes its own message, with the hours left, for the bound of 5 a day.
  passkey_limit: "You have 10 passkeys. Remove one to add another.",
  passkey_suspended: "This passkey was switched off because a copy of it may exist. Remove it and add a new one.",
  passkey_not_found: "That passkey is gone.",
  challenge_expired: "That took too long. Try again.",
  // 3e (design, section 9.5): a handle korbat retired, refused to everyone, its former holder included.
  handle_retired: "That handle was retired by korbat. Nobody can use it.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  // The staff console's (3a design, section 10). Where only the operator can help, they say so; none sends the person to
  // a remedy the console does not have, which is why the staff flows never answer a passkey_* code.
  staff_session_required: "Your staff session ended. Sign in with your staff key.",
  staff_key_invalid: "This key does not open the staff console. If it should, ask the operator to check your staff keys.",
  staff_key_suspended: "This staff key was switched off because a copy of it may exist. Ask the operator for a link to enrol a new one.",
  staff_key_limit: "This account has 5 staff keys. Ask the operator to revoke one before enrolling another.",
  staff_key_not_device_bound: "This key can be synced or copied, so it cannot be a staff key. Use a security key or a device-bound authenticator.",
  staff_key_not_user_verified: "This key did not ask for a PIN or fingerprint, so it cannot be a staff key. Set a PIN on it, or use another key.",
  staff_key_refused: "The browser's answer for this key could not be checked. Try again, or use another key; this link still works.",
  staff_enrollment_invalid: "This enrolment link has expired or was already used. Ask the operator for a new one.",
  staff_step_up_required: "Confirm this with your staff key.",
  staff_step_up_invalid: "That confirmation was for another action, was already used or could not be checked. Try again.",
};

export function authErrorMessage(code: AuthErrorKind): string {
  return MESSAGES[code];
}

/** An expected, user-facing failure. The HTTP layer turns it into an ErrorEnvelope with this code and status. */
export class AuthError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: AuthErrorKind,
    readonly status: AuthErrorStatus,
    message: string = MESSAGES[code],
    /** For rate limits: seconds until the window resets, sent as Retry-After. */
    readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number,
    /**
     * What the app needs beyond the code, sent as the envelope's `details`: for reauth_required, the level the action
     * asks for and the factor kinds the session proved in time (1c design, section 7.1).
     */
    readonly details?: Record<string, unknown>,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "AuthError";
  }
}

/**
 * The code the database's guard of handles raised (3e design, section 6.2, profiles_handle_guard), however deeply the driver
 * error is wrapped: `handle_retired` or `handle_reserved` under SQLSTATE P0001, else null. The flows check both first, to
 * answer with a code; this is what a write that lost a race meets, and its caller answers the same.
 */
export function handleRefusal(err: unknown): "handle_retired" | "handle_reserved" | null {
  let current: unknown = err;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current; depth++) {
    if (typeof current === "object" && (current as { code?: unknown }).code === "P0001") {
      const message = (current as { message?: unknown }).message;
      return message === "handle_retired" || message === "handle_reserved" ? message : null;
    }
    current = (current as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  }
  return null;
}

/** True for a Postgres unique-constraint violation, however deeply the driver error is wrapped. */
export function isUniqueViolation(err: unknown): boolean {
  let current: unknown = err;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current; depth++) {
    if (typeof current === "object" && (current as { code?: unknown }).code === "23505") return true;
    current = (current as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  }
  return false;
}
```

```ts
import type { OnboardingHandleRequest, Profile, SignupCompleteRequest } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { meetsMinimumAge } from "../age";
import { AuthError, isUniqueViolation, type AuthDeps, type RequestContext } from "../context";
import { checkHandle } from "../handles";
import { emailHash } from "../identifiers";
import { HOUR, enforceLimit } from "../limits";
import type { IssuedSession, Session } from "../sessions";
import { ageBlockKey, signupKey, type PendingSignup } from "./email";
import { signIn, type SignedIn } from "./signin";

export const AGE_BLOCK_MS = 24 * HOUR;

/**
 * Creates the account after a verified sign-up code. Terms and age are checked first; an under-16
 * date of birth stores nothing, blocks this email for 24 hours and ends the flow. Date of birth is
 * never written anywhere.
 */
export async function completeSignup(deps: AuthDeps, input: SignupCompleteRequest, ctx: RequestContext): Promise<SignedIn> {
  await enforceLimit(deps.kv, `signup-complete:ip:${ctx.ipHash}`, 10, HOUR);
  const raw = await deps.kv.get(signupKey(input.flowId));
  if (!raw) throw new AuthError("invalid_code", 400);
  const pending = JSON.parse(raw) as PendingSignup;

  if (input.termsVersion !== deps.config.termsVersion) throw new AuthError("terms_required", 400);

  if (!meetsMinimumAge(input.dateOfBirth, deps.now())) {
    await deps.kv.del(signupKey(input.flowId));
    await deps.kv.set(ageBlockKey(emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, pending.email)), "1", AGE_BLOCK_MS);
    throw new AuthError("age_requirement", 403);
  }

  if (!(await deps.kv.take(signupKey(input.flowId)))) throw new AuthError("invalid_code", 400);

  let user;
  try {
    user = await deps.repo.createUser({ email: pending.email, termsVersion: input.termsVersion, now: deps.now() });
  } catch (err) {
    if (isUniqueViolation(err)) throw new AuthError("invalid_code", 400, "An account with this email already exists. Sign in instead.");
    throw err;
  }
  await deps.repo.appendEvent({ userId: user.id, type: "signup", ipHash: ctx.ipHash });
  // The sign-up code proved the address: the first session's email factor, at the flows' clock.
  return signIn(deps, user, { deviceId: pending.deviceId, platform: pending.platform }, ctx, { alertNewDevice: false, factors: { email: deps.now().getTime() }, method: "email" });
}

/** Onboarding: claims a handle, marks the account onboarded and swaps the onboarding session for a full one. */
export async function chooseHandle(
  deps: AuthDeps,
  session: Session,
  input: OnboardingHandleRequest,
): Promise<{ profile: Profile; issued: IssuedSession }> {
  await enforceLimit(deps.kv, `onboarding-handle:${session.sessionId}`, 10, HOUR);
  if (session.onboarded) throw new AuthError("handle_taken", 409, "Your profile already exists.");
  const problem = checkHandle(input.handle);
  if (problem) throw new AuthError(problem, 400);
  const created = await deps.profiles.create({ id: session.userId, handle: input.handle, displayName: input.displayName });
  if (!created.ok) {
    // 3e: a handle korbat retired is refused as one another profile holds (409); one of the placeholder's form, which
    // checkHandle refuses first, reaches the database's guard only from a caller that skipped it (400).
    if (created.reason === "handle_reserved") throw new AuthError("handle_reserved", 400);
    throw new AuthError(created.reason, 409);
  }
  await deps.repo.markOnboarded(session.userId, deps.now());
  const issued = await deps.sessions.rotate(session);
  return { profile: created.profile, issued };
}
```

```ts
import { RETIRED_HANDLE_PREFIX } from "@korbat/contracts";

export const RESERVED_HANDLES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  "admin",
  "administrator",
  "korbat",
  "support",
  "help",
  "moderator",
  "mod",
  "staff",
  "security",
  "root",
  "system",
  "official",
  "api",
  "www",
  "about",
  "rules",
  "transparency",
  "settings",
]);

export type HandleError = "handle_invalid" | "handle_reserved";

/**
 * Handles are 3-20 of a-z, 0-9 and underscore, and not reserved. Input is expected already lowercased. The whole prefix of
 * a retired handle's placeholder is reserved (3e design, section 7.10 item 4), not only its exact form, so no handle
 * anyone chooses can pass for an account whose handle korbat retired.
 */
export function checkHandle(handle: string): HandleError | null {
  if (!/^[a-z0-9_]{3,20}$/.test(handle)) return "handle_invalid";
  if (RESERVED_HANDLES.has(handle) || handle.startsWith(RETIRED_HANDLE_PREFIX)) return "handle_reserved";
  return null;
}
```

```ts
export interface CreateAuthOptions {
  config: Config;
  logger: Logger;
  /** The korbat_auth pool. The auth module never receives the API pool. */
  authDb: Db;
  mailer: Mailer;
  profiles: ProfileStore;
  /** Either a Redis client or a ready key-value store (tests use an in-memory store). */
  redis?: Redis;
  kv?: KeyValueStore;
  turnstile?: TurnstileVerifier;
  breachChecker?: BreachChecker;
  /**
   * The phone verification provider behind the verified badge. Absent or null, the badge routes answer
   * badge_unavailable; the server passes verificationProviderFrom(config), tests the development provider.
   */
  verify?: VerificationProvider | null;
  now?: () => Date;
}

/**
 * The provider VERIFY_PROVIDER names: none for `off` (the badge is hidden), the fixed-code one for `dev`,
 * Vonage Verify with the configured credentials and brand for `vonage`. `fetchFn` is for tests only.
 */
export function verificationProviderFrom(config: Config, fetchFn?: typeof fetch): VerificationProvider | null {
  switch (config.VERIFY_PROVIDER) {
    case "off":
      return null;
    case "dev":
      return devProvider();
    case "vonage":
      // Production refuses this configuration in config.ts; development gets the same refusal here, at start-up, rather than a failing first request.
      if (!config.VONAGE_API_KEY || !config.VONAGE_API_SECRET) throw new Error("VERIFY_PROVIDER=vonage needs VONAGE_API_KEY and VONAGE_API_SECRET");
      return vonageProvider({ apiKey: config.VONAGE_API_KEY, apiSecret: config.VONAGE_API_SECRET, brand: config.VERIFY_BRAND, fetch: fetchFn });
  }
}

export function createAuth(options: CreateAuthOptions) {
  const kv = options.kv ?? (options.redis ? redisKv(options.redis) : undefined);
  if (!kv) throw new Error("createAuth needs a Redis client or a key-value store");
  const now = options.now ?? (() => new Date());
  const repo = createAuthRepo(options.authDb);
  const sessions = createSessions({ repo, kv, now });
  const deps: AuthDeps = {
    repo,
    kv,
    sessions,
    lockout: createLockout({ repo, kv, now }),
    mailer: options.mailer,
    turnstile: options.turnstile ?? cloudflareTurnstile(options.config.TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY),
    breachChecker: options.breachChecker ?? hibpChecker(),
    profiles: options.profiles,
    verify: options.verify ?? null,
    config: authConfigFrom(options.config),
    log: options.logger,
    now,
  };
  /** A security event about an account, for the modules that own no auth table (the social module's profile and handle changes, the account module's export). */
  const appendEvent = (userId: string, type: AuthEventType, metadata?: Record<string, unknown>) => repo.appendEvent({ userId, type, metadata });
  const forAccount: AuthForAccount = {
    startDeletion: (session, ctx) => startDeletion(deps, session, ctx),
    confirmDeletion: (session, input) => confirmDeletion(deps, session, input),
    pendingPurges: () => repo.pendingPurges(),
    finishPurge: (userId) => finishPurge(deps, userId),
    exportAccount: (userId) => exportAccount(deps, userId),
    appendEvent,
  };
  const staffGuard = requireStaff(deps);
  const forStaff: AuthForStaff = {
    enrollOptions: (input) => enrollOptions(deps, input),
    enrollVerify: (input, ctx) => enrollVerify(deps, input, ctx),
    signInOptions: () => signInOptions(deps),
    signInVerify: (input, ctx) => signInVerify(deps, input, ctx),
    requireStaff: staffGuard,
    me: (session) => staffMe(deps, session),
    sessions: (session) => listStaffSessions(deps, session),
    keys: (session) => listStaffKeys(deps, session),
    signOut: (session, ctx) => signOutStaff(deps, session, ctx),
    stepUpOptions: (session, request) => stepUpOptions(deps, session, request),
    requireStaffStepUp: (action, target) => requireStaffStepUp(deps, action, target),
    revokeSession: (session, confirmed, ctx) => revokeStaffSession(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
  };
  const forModeration: AuthForModeration = {
    verifyHuman: (token) => deps.turnstile.verify(token),
    storeNotifierContact: (contactId, contact) => storeNotifierContact(deps, contactId, contact),
    mailNotifier: (contactId, message) => mailNotifier(deps, contactId, message),
    mailAccount: (userId, message) => mailAccount(deps, userId, message),
    mailNotifierUpdates: (parts) => mailNotifierUpdates(deps, parts),
    mailStaff: (message) => mailStaff(deps, message),
    notifierFacts: (contactIds) => notifierFacts(deps, contactIds),
    notifierName: (contactId) => notifierName(deps, contactId),
    notifierMailTokenMatches: (contactId, token) => notifierMailTokenMatches(deps, contactId, token),
    confirmNotifier: (contactId, token) => confirmNotifier(deps, contactId, token),
    stopNotifier: (contactId, token) => stopNotifier(deps, contactId, token),
    accountReportMailStopped: (userId) => accountReportMailStopped(deps, userId),
    resumeAccountReportMail: (userId) => resumeAccountReportMail(deps, userId),
    forgetNotifierAfter: (contactIds, at) => forgetNotifierAfter(deps, contactIds, at),
    findNotifierContacts: (email) => findNotifierContacts(deps, email),
    overdueContacts: () => overdueContacts(deps),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    routes: authRoutes(deps),
    me: meHandler(deps),
    appendEvent,
    /** The interface the account module uses. */
    forAccount,
    /** The interface the staff module uses. */
    forStaff,
    /** The interface the moderation module uses. */
    forModeration,
    /** Runs first on every request: resolves the client address the way TRUST_PROXY says and hashes it, and its network with it. */
    clientIdentity: clientIdentity({ trust: deps.config.trustProxy, ipHashKey: deps.config.ipHashKey }),
    resolveSession: resolveSession(deps),
    requireSession,
    requireOnboarding,
    requireFreshAuth: (maxAgeSeconds?: number) => requireFreshAuth(deps, maxAgeSeconds),
    /** Level 2 within the window on an account with TOTP, level 1 otherwise: for the routes of the 1c design's section 10. */
    requireStrongFreshAuth: (maxAgeSeconds?: number) => requireStrongFreshAuth(deps, maxAgeSeconds),
    /** A staff session from the staff cookie, read from the database at every request (3a design, section 7). */
    requireStaff: staffGuard,
    /** A fresh confirmation by the staff session's key, bound to the action a route is about to execute (3a design, section 7). */
    requireStaffStepUp: forStaff.requireStaffStepUp,
    /** Starts the retention pass (dead codes, old sessions and staff sessions, spent enrolment links, device address hashes, old events, forgotten notifier contacts and their confirmations) and returns the function that stops it. */
    startJanitor: (lock: JobLock) => createJanitor(deps, lock).start(),
  };
}

export type Auth = ReturnType<typeof createAuth>;
```

```ts
/**
 * The queue and the case, for staff (3c design, section 7.3): the overview the home screen shows, the queue, the case
 * answer, the one door to a case's images, a fresh snapshot, and a moderator's own finding. Every read of a case is
 * written to the access log and counts against the day's limit; none of it needs the key.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the day, and the bands of a reporter's summary

/** How many seconds are left to midnight UTC, at least one: what a refusal at a daily limit tells the console to wait. */
export function secondsToUtcMidnight(now: Date): number {
  const midnight = Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear(), now.getUTCMonth(), now.getUTCDate() + 1);
  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil((midnight - now.getTime()) / 1000));
}

/** The same moment `months` calendar months later in UTC; a day the target month lacks becomes that month's last day. */
function monthsAfter(at: Date, months: number): Date {
  const month = at.getUTCMonth() + months;
  const lastDay = new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate();
  return new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month, Math.min(at.getUTCDate(), lastDay), at.getUTCHours(), at.getUTCMinutes(), at.getUTCSeconds(), at.getUTCMilliseconds()));
}

/** A reporter's account age as a band: under one month, one to twelve months (both ends included), or over twelve. */
export function accountAgeBand(createdAt: Date, now: Date): NonNullable<SourceSummary["accountAge"]> {
  if (now.getTime() < monthsAfter(createdAt, 1).getTime()) return "under_1_month";
  return now.getTime() <= monthsAfter(createdAt, 12).getTime() ? "1_to_12_months" : "over_12_months";
}

/** How many items a reporter filed, the one being read included, as a band. */
export function itemsFiledBand(filed: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["itemsFiled"]> {
  if (filed <= 1) return "1";
  return filed <= 9 ? "2_to_9" : "10_or_more";
}

/** The share of a reporter's decided items that were acted on, as a band; exactly half is "half or more". */
export function actedOnBand(decided: number, actedOn: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["actedOn"]> {
  if (decided <= 0) return "none_decided";
  if (actedOn <= 0) return "none";
  return actedOn * 2 < decided ? "under_half" : "half_or_more";
}

/** How many of a reporter's items were answered while nobody could open the images, as a band; they are counted apart from the decided ones. */
export function answeredUnseenBand(unseen: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["answeredUnseen"]> {
  if (unseen <= 0) return "none";
  if (unseen === 1) return "1";
  return unseen <= 9 ? "2_to_9" : "10_or_more";
}

/**
 * Each reporter's place among the reporters of one case, from 0, in the order of each one's first item in the case: the
 * letter the case page gives them. Given per case, so one person's letter on one case says nothing about another.
 */
export function reporterIndexes(reportersInItemOrder: readonly (string | null)[]): Map<string, number> {
  const indexes = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const reporter of reportersInItemOrder) if (reporter !== null && !indexes.has(reporter)) indexes.set(reporter, indexes.size);
  return indexes;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- recusal

/**
 * Refuses a staff account that is too close to the case's subject: every route that names a case, or an item of one,
 * asks this first, so a refused read writes no access row and does not count against the day's limit. The check never
 * looks at who reported, and its answer reads the same whoever the conflict concerns.
 */
export async function refuseRecused(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<void> {
  if (await staffCaseConflict(deps.apiDb, session.userId, caseId)) throw new ModerationError("staff_recused");
}

/** The case, after the recusal check; not_found when no case has the id. */
async function openableCase(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseRow> {
  await refuseRecused(deps, session, caseId);
  const row = await caseById(deps.apiDb, caseId);
  if (!row) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  return row;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the overview

/** The reading person as the review marks ask about them: the session's account, and whether its role is admin. */
export const reviewerOf = (session: ActiveStaffSession) => ({ id: session.userId, admin: session.role === "admin" });

/** How long the overview's late erasures are kept before they are read again. */
export const ERASURE_OVERDUE_TTL_MS = 60_000;

/** The late erasures last read on a pool, and when: one read serves every staff member's home screen for a minute. */
const lateByPool = new WeakMap<object, { at: number; counts: Promise<ErasureOverdue> }>();

/**
 * The overview's erasureOverdue (3c design, section 7.3): one count for each due rule of what a step of the retention
 * job or the auth janitor should have changed more than a day ago and has not. The image rows are the media module's to
 * count and the notifiers' contacts the auth module's, since this module names neither.
 *
 * The counts are read at most once a minute for all staff, and a read in flight is shared: the count of late image rows
 * reads the freeze once for each kept row of a frozen account's deleted posts (seconds at twenty thousand rows), which a
 * home screen must not pay on every load, and both jobs run only every ten minutes, so a count a minute old says the
 * same. A read that failed is not kept.
 */
export function erasureOverdue(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "auth" | "now">): Promise<ErasureOverdue> {
  const now = deps.now().getTime();
  const kept = lateByPool.get(deps.apiDb);
  if (kept && now >= kept.at && now - kept.at < ERASURE_OVERDUE_TTL_MS) return kept.counts;
  const counts = (async (): Promise<ErasureOverdue> => {
    const late = await lateErasures(deps.apiDb, RETENTION);
    return { ...late, images: await deps.media.overdueDeletions(), contacts: await deps.auth.overdueContacts() };
  })();
  lateByPool.set(deps.apiDb, { at: now, counts });
  counts.catch(() => {
    if (lateByPool.get(deps.apiDb)?.counts === counts) lateByPool.delete(deps.apiDb);
  });
  return counts;
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/overview: counts, times, staff handles and cases, for every staff member's home screen. One number is
 * the reading person's own: how many of the waiting appeals they may review.
 */
export async function overview(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config" | "media" | "auth" | "now">, session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffOverview> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;
  const byLane = await openByLane(q);
  const today = await staffToday(q);
  const mails = await mailAndReleaseCounts(q, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
  const appeals = await appealCounts(q, reviewerOf(session));
  return {
    lanes: ([0, 1, 2] as const).map((lane) => byLane.find((row) => row.lane === lane) ?? { lane, open: 0, oldestAt: null }),
    appealsWaiting: appeals.waiting,
    appealsYouMayReview: appeals.mayReview,
    appealsWithoutReviewer: appeals.withoutReviewer,
    reveals: await recentReveals(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    imagesToday: today.images,
    findingsToday: today.findings,
    mailsWaiting: mails.waiting,
    mailsFailed: mails.failed,
    releaseOverdue: mails.releaseOverdue,
    erasureOverdue: await erasureOverdue(deps),
    deferUnproven: deps.config.MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN === "on",
    // The three lists of the path for child sexual abuse material, which every staff member sees: what lifted the
    // protection of reported images, who chose not to seal, and which seals taken while deciding stand.
    protectionLifted: await recentProtectionLifted(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    sealsDeclined: await recentSealsDeclined(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    interimSeals: await interimSealsInForce(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the queue

const CURSOR_TIME = /^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}[.][0-9]{6}Z$/;
const CURSOR_ID = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;

/** The queue's cursor: the last row's sort key as an opaque word. */
const encodeCursor = (row: QueueCursor): string => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify([row.lane, row.deferred, row.sortAt, row.id]), "utf8").toString("base64url");

/** Reads a cursor back; anything this module did not write is refused, never guessed at. */
function decodeCursor(cursor: string): QueueCursor {
  let parts: unknown;
  try {
    parts = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(cursor, "base64url").toString("utf8"));
  } catch {
    throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(parts) || parts.length !== 4) throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  const [lane, deferred, sortAt, id] = parts as unknown[];
  if ((lane !== 0 && lane !== 1 && lane !== 2) || typeof deferred !== "boolean" || typeof sortAt !== "string" || !CURSOR_TIME.test(sortAt) || typeof id !== "string" || !CURSOR_ID.test(id)) {
    throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  }
  return { lane, deferred, sortAt, id };
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/queue: open cases by lane and age, 50 a page. Only under the emergency switch are cases whose unanswered
 * items all come from unproven sources sorted after the others of their lane, never below a less severe lane.
 */
export async function queue(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config">, cursor?: string): Promise<QueuePage> {
  const after = cursor === undefined ? null : decodeCursor(cursor);
  const found = await queueRows(deps.apiDb, { deferUnproven: deps.config.MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN === "on", after, limit: QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE + 1 });
  const page = found.slice(0, QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE);
  const last = page.at(-1);
  return {
    cases: page.map(
      (row): QueueRow => ({
        id: row.id,
        lane: row.lane,
        targetType: row.targetType,
        openedAt: row.openedAt,
        oldestOpenAt: row.oldestOpenAt,
        openItems: row.openItems,
        rules: row.rules as QueueRow["rules"],
        categories: row.categories as QueueRow["categories"],
        allegesIllegal: row.allegesIllegal,
        suspect: row.suspect,
        reexamination: row.reexamination,
        deferred: row.deferred,
      }),
    ),
    // One row more than the page was read: only then is there a next page.
    nextCursor: found.length > QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE && last ? encodeCursor(last) : null,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the case answer

/** A snapshot as the case answer carries it: its content unless the database's one predicate withholds it. */
function snapshotView(snapshot: SnapshotRead): CaseSnapshot {
  if (snapshot.withheld || snapshot.salt === null) return { id: snapshot.id, takenAt: snapshot.takenAt, digest: snapshot.digest, withheld: true };
  return {
    id: snapshot.id,
    takenAt: snapshot.takenAt,
    digest: snapshot.digest,
    withheld: false,
    salt: snapshot.salt,
    targetType: snapshot.targetType,
    targetId: snapshot.targetId,
    authorHandle: snapshot.authorHandle,
    postState: snapshot.postState,
    postCreatedAt: snapshot.postCreatedAt,
    replyToId: snapshot.replyToId,
    quoteOfId: snapshot.quoteOfId,
    body: snapshot.body,
    media: snapshot.media,
    displayName: snapshot.displayName,
    bio: snapshot.bio,
    handle: snapshot.handle,
  };
}

const NO_BANDS = { accountAge: null, itemsFiled: null, actedOn: null, answeredUnseen: null } as const;
const NO_CONTACT = { named: null, contactGiven: null, confirmed: null, suppressed: null, contactLost: false } as const;

/**
 * Who sent an item, as a summary that names nobody (3c design, section 7.3). A finding was found by a moderator; a notice
 * on the path for child sexual abuse material is anonymous, whoever sent it; a signed-out notifier is what the auth
 * module says of the contact, never the contact; a signed-in reporter is a letter and four bands, or, once the link to
 * the account is gone, only that.
 */
function sourceOf(item: CaseItemRow, letters: Map<string, number>, reporters: Map<string, ReporterFacts>, contacts: Map<string, NotifierFacts>, now: Date): SourceSummary {
  if (item.intakeKind === "finding") return { kind: "staff", label: SOURCE_LABELS.staff, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  if (item.csam) return { kind: "anonymous", label: SOURCE_LABELS.anonymous, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  if (item.channel === "signed_out") {
    const facts = item.contactId === null ? undefined : contacts.get(item.contactId);
    return {
      kind: "notifier",
      label: SOURCE_LABELS.notifier,
      ...NO_BANDS,
      named: facts?.named ?? false,
      contactGiven: facts?.contactGiven ?? false,
      confirmed: facts?.confirmed ?? false,
      suppressed: facts?.suppressed ?? false,
      // The notice left a contact that the auth module no longer has: never stored, or forgotten since.
      contactLost: item.contactId !== null && !(facts?.found ?? false),
    };
  }
  if (item.reporterAccountId === null) return { kind: "unlinked", label: SOURCE_LABELS.unlinked, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  const facts = reporters.get(item.reporterAccountId);
  return {
    kind: "reporter",
    label: reporterLabel(letters.get(item.reporterAccountId) ?? 0),
    accountAge: facts?.createdAt ? accountAgeBand(facts.createdAt, now) : null,
    itemsFiled: itemsFiledBand(facts?.filed ?? 1),
    actedOn: actedOnBand(facts?.decided ?? 0, facts?.actedOn ?? 0),
    answeredUnseen: answeredUnseenBand(facts?.answeredUnseen ?? 0),
    ...NO_CONTACT,
  };
}

/** Whether an item's source is a signed-in reporter still linked to an account: the only items that get a letter. */
const linkedReporter = (item: CaseItemRow): string | null => (item.intakeKind === "user" && !item.csam && item.channel === "signed_in" ? item.reporterAccountId : null);

/**
 * The case as staff read it: what is, never what its senders are told (the status page keeps a live target from a dead
 * one; this answer does not). It writes nothing: readCase logs the read and holds it to the day's limit.
 */
export async function caseView(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "media" | "config" | "now">, session: ActiveStaffSession, row: CaseRow): Promise<CaseView> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;
  const origin = deps.config.APP_ORIGIN;

  // The target as it stands. An account case shows no image: a profile holds none, and the images of its posts are shown
  // only on those posts' own cases.
  let target: CaseTarget;
  let imagesAllowed = false;
  let authorId: string | null;
  if (row.targetType === "post") {
    const post = await livePost(q, row.targetId);
    target = { type: "post", id: row.targetId, link: postLink(origin, row.targetId), authorHandle: post?.authorHandle ?? null, state: post?.state ?? null, level: post?.level ?? null };
    imagesAllowed = post?.imagesAllowed ?? false;
    authorId = post?.authorId ?? null;
  } else {
    const account = await liveAccount(q, row.targetId);
    target = { type: "account", id: row.targetId, handle: account?.handle ?? null, displayName: account?.displayName ?? null, bio: account?.bio ?? null, deleted: account?.deleted ?? false };
    authorId = row.targetId;
  }

  // What the page shows in place of images on the path for child sexual abuse material: counts and days only.
  const marks = await suspicionOf(q, row.id);
  let suspicion: CaseView["suspicion"] = null;
  if (marks.holds) {
    const reach = await deps.media.reach({ type: row.targetType, id: row.targetId });
    const earlier = await earlierAnswers(q, { type: row.targetType, id: row.targetId }, authorId, SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS);
    suspicion = {
      open: marks.open,
      reach: { posts: reach.posts, images: reach.images, sealed: reach.sealed, served: reach.served, newestPostOn: reach.newestPostOn },
      // Only a post's images are ever shown in the console, so only a post's case can say when staff last looked.
      earlier: { target: { ...earlier.target, imagesOpenedOn: row.targetType === "post" ? await imagesOpenedOn(q, row.targetId) : null }, author: earlier.author },
    };
  }

  const itemRows = await caseItems(q, row.id, session.userId);
  const letters = reporterIndexes(itemRows.map(linkedReporter));
  const reporters = await reporterFacts(q, [...letters.keys()]);
  const contactIds = [...new Set(itemRows.flatMap((item) => (item.channel === "signed_out" && !item.csam && item.contactId !== null ? [item.contactId] : [])))];
  const contacts = contactIds.length === 0 ? new Map<string, NotifierFacts>() : await deps.auth.notifierFacts(contactIds);
  const now = deps.now();
  const items = itemRows.map(
    (item): CaseItem => ({
      id: item.id,
      seq: item.seq,
      position: item.position,
      createdAt: item.createdAt,
      lane: item.lane,
      // An account's address is built from the handle as it was named; the target above carries the handle it holds now.
      link: item.targetType === "post" ? postLink(origin, item.targetId) : accountLink(origin, item.namedHandle ?? ""),
      ruleId: item.ruleId as CaseItem["ruleId"],
      allegesIllegal: item.allegesIllegal,
      csam: item.csam,
      category: item.category as CaseItem["category"],
      categoryKeyword: item.categoryKeyword,
      citedLaw: item.citedLaw,
      explanation: item.explanation,
      mediaId: item.mediaId,
      suspect: item.suspect,
      // An item korbat added for a quoted post stands ten positions after the item it was added for.
      quotedByPosition: item.position > 10 ? item.position - 10 : null,
      quotedCaseId: item.quotedCaseId,
      reexaminesPosition: item.reexaminesPosition,
      reexaminesYourDecision: item.reexaminesYourDecision,
      statement: item.statement,
      outcome: item.outcome as CaseItem["outcome"],
      answeredBy: item.answeredBy,
      erased: item.erased,
      source: sourceOf(item, letters, reporters, contacts, now),
    }),
  );

  const actions = await caseActions(q, row.id);
  // The columns of 3e of every ledger row of the case, with a standing measure's period as it stands now.
  const columns = await standingColumns(q, row.id);
  const decisions: CaseDecision[] = [];
  for (const decision of await caseDecisions(q, row.id)) {
    const own: CaseDecision["actions"] = [];
    for (const action of actions.filter((candidate) => candidate.decisionId === decision.id)) {
      const more = columns.get(action.id);
      own.push({
        id: action.id,
        kind: action.kind,
        mediaId: action.mediaId,
        noEffect: action.noEffect,
        inForce: action.inForce,
        reversesActionId: action.reversesActionId,
        liftedBy: action.liftedBy,
        // A seal's list is the database's, written when the seal was recorded: text for the report to the police.
        sealed: action.kind === "seal_media" ? await sealCovers(q, action.id, SEAL_LIST_MAX) : null,
        days: more?.days ?? null,
        announced: more?.announced ?? null,
        basis: (more?.basis ?? null) as CaseDecisionAction["basis"],
        restsOn: more?.restsOn ?? null,
        earliestStart: more?.earliestStart ?? null,
        countsUntil: more?.countsUntil ?? null,
        period: (more?.period ?? null) as CaseDecisionAction["period"],
        restedOnBy: (more?.restedOnBy ?? null) as CaseDecisionAction["restedOnBy"],
        // 3e Task 2: a retirement names the handle it retired; no other row carries the member.
        ...(more?.handle ? { handle: more.handle } : {}),
      });
    }
    decisions.push({
      id: decision.id,
      kind: decision.kind,
      outcome: decision.outcome as CaseDecision["outcome"],
      ground: decision.ground as CaseDecision["ground"],
      ruleId: decision.ruleId as CaseDecision["ruleId"],
      rulesVersion: decision.rulesVersion,
      redressVersion: decision.redressVersion,
      category: decision.category as CaseDecision["category"],
      categoryKeyword: decision.categoryKeyword,
      source: decision.source as CaseDecision["source"],
      decidedAt: decision.decidedAt,
      staffHandle: decision.staffHandle,
      throughSeq: decision.throughSeq,
      answersFromSeq: decision.answersFromSeq,
      reviewsDecisionId: decision.reviewsDecisionId,
      snapshotId: decision.snapshotId,
      suspect: decision.suspect,
      unseen: decision.unseen,
      needsAdmin: decision.needsAdmin,
      endedInterim: decision.endedInterim,
      facts: decision.facts,
      reason: decision.reason,
      legalReference: decision.legalReference,
      actions: own,
    });
  }

  const texts = await caseStaffTexts(q, row.id);
  const staffText = (text: (typeof texts)[number]) => ({ id: text.id, staffHandle: text.staffHandle, createdAt: text.createdAt, text: text.text });
  return {
    id: row.id,
    lane: row.lane,
    stateVersion: row.stateVersion,
    intakeSeq: row.intakeSeq,
    answeredSeq: row.answeredSeq,
    openedAt: row.openedAt,
    closedAt: row.closedAt,
    target,
    suspicion,
    imagesAllowed,
    snapshots: (await caseSnapshots(q, row.id)).map(snapshotView),
    items,
    decisions,
    appeals: await caseAppeals(q, row.id, reviewerOf(session)),
    drafts: (await ownDrafts(q, row.id, session.userId)) as StaffTextDraft[],
    notes: texts.filter((text) => text.kind === "note").map(staffText),
    sealsDeclined: texts.filter((text) => text.kind === "seal_declined").map(staffText),
    history: (await caseHistory(q, row.id)) as CaseHistoryEntry[],
    // 3e: on a post case whether a final restriction gives a strike and its author's standing in bands (the author of a
    // post that is gone has none to show); on an account case the account's standing.
    strikeDue: row.targetType === "post" ? await strikeDue(q, row.id) : null,
    authorStanding: row.targetType === "post" && authorId !== null ? await authorStanding(q, authorId) : null,
    standing: row.targetType === "account" ? await caseStanding(q, row.id, row.targetId) : null,
  };
}

/** The alert's key for one staff account's day: its window ends at midnight UTC, so the alert goes once that day. */
const readsKey = (staffId: string) => `moderation-reads:${staffId}`;

/**
 * Tells every staff account, the person's own included, that a staff account reached the day's limit on cases: a stolen
 * key reads at the speed of requests, and this mail is how the others learn of it. Once a day for each account.
 */
async function alertDailyReads(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log" | "now">, staffId: string, limit: number): Promise<void> {
  const handle = (await handleOf(deps.apiDb, staffId)) ?? "unknown";
  await staffAlert(deps, readsKey(staffId), secondsToUtcMidnight(deps.now()) * 1000, { template: "moderation_reads", handle, limit });
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/cases/:case. In this order: the recusal check; the day's limit, which counts different cases, so a case
 * the person already opened today is never refused and a reload or a decision's answer never meets it; the access row;
 * then the answer. A person at the limit is refused every other case until midnight UTC, with nothing written, and every
 * staff account is told once that day.
 */
export async function readCase(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseView> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  const limits = await dailyLimits(deps.apiDb);
  const opened = await casesOpenedToday(deps.apiDb, session.userId, caseId);
  if (!opened.thisCase && opened.cases >= limits.caseOpens) {
    deps.background.start(() => alertDailyReads(deps, session.userId, limits.caseOpens));
    throw new ModerationError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, secondsToUtcMidnight(deps.now()));
  }
  await insertAccess(deps.apiDb, { staffId: session.userId, caseId, kind: "case_opened" });
  return caseView(deps, session, row);
}

/**
 * The case as the answer to a decision the person's key has just confirmed on it (3c design, section 7.5, step 4): the
 * read is written to the access log like every read of a case, and it is not held to the day's limit on different
 * cases, which counts openings. A decision's answer is no opening of another case: its person has just acted on this
 * one, and the decision's own caps bound how often that can be. So no committed decision is answered with a refusal.
 */
export async function readDecidedCase(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseView> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  await insertAccess(deps.apiDb, { staffId: session.userId, caseId, kind: "case_opened" });
  return caseView(deps, session, row);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- images in the console

/**
 * GET /api/staff/cases/:case/media/:media/:size: an image of the case's own post, opened for staff, or image_refused. The
 * media module's one function decides what may be opened at all (gate V: never a sealed or an erased image, never an
 * image of a frozen post, on whatever case, open or closed); this route adds that the image is the case's. In this order:
 *   1. the recusal check and the case, as on every case route; only a post's case shows images;
 *   2. the image is one that a snapshot of the case lists, while that snapshot still holds its content: read from the
 *      module's own evidence, before the media module is asked. An id that names nothing and an id of another post's image
 *      are then refused by the same steps, with no file looked for, so the time an answer takes tells the two apart no
 *      more than the answer does;
 *   3. the media module's answer, and that the image it opened is on the case's own post.
 * Every refusal reads the same, and the file's handle is closed on each refusal after the open. Each view is written to
 * the access log before a byte is sent. The caller streams the file and closes it.
 */
export async function caseImage(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string, mediaId: string, size: MediaSize): Promise<StoredFile> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  if (row.targetType !== "post") throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
  // The id in the spelling the database writes, which is the one a snapshot lists its images by.
  const imageId = mediaId.toLowerCase();
  if (!(await snapshotListsImage(deps.apiDb, caseId, imageId))) throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
  const image = await deps.media.staffImage(imageId, size);
  if (!image) throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
  try {
    // The image is of another post than this case's: the same answer as for an image that is not shown at all.
    if (image.postId !== row.targetId) throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
    await insertAccess(deps.apiDb, { staffId: session.userId, caseId, kind: "image_viewed", mediaId: imageId });
  } catch (err) {
    await image.file.handle.close();
    throw err;
  }
  return image.file;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- a fresh snapshot

/** The longest one run of the snapshot route waits for a lock: the post's row or the case's, which a decision holds while it is recorded. */
const SNAPSHOT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

/** Whether a stored snapshot holds exactly what a capture holds now. */
function sameContent(stored: SnapshotRead, live: SnapshotContent): boolean {
  const images = (list: SnapshotContent["media"]) => JSON.stringify((list ?? []).map((image) => [image.id, image.alt, image.width, image.height]));
  return (
    stored.authorHandle === live.authorHandle &&
    stored.postState === live.postState &&
    stored.postCreatedAt === live.postCreatedAt &&
    stored.replyToId === live.replyToId &&
    stored.quoteOfId === live.quoteOfId &&
    stored.body === live.body &&
    (stored.media === null) === (live.media === null) &&
    images(stored.media) === images(live.media) &&
    stored.displayName === live.displayName &&
    stored.bio === live.bio &&
    stored.handle === live.handle
  );
}

/**
 * How often the snapshot's transaction is run again after a deadlock or a lock timeout, as an intake's is: in each run
 * that gave way nothing was written.
 */
const SNAPSHOT_RETRIES = 3;

/**
 * POST /api/staff/cases/:case/snapshots: a fresh snapshot of the target as it stands, taken the intake's way (a post under
 * a share lock with its images under their row locks, held for the case; a tombstone for a deleted post; no content after
 * an erasure), when it differs from the case's newest one or that one is withheld or erased. It answers the new
 * snapshot's id and digest, or the newest one's when nothing differed, never content: the console reads the case again,
 * so every read of a case's content goes through that route's access row and the day's limit. It needs no key: it changes
 * nothing a user sees, and enters the record only through a decision that names it.
 *
 * Its locks come in another order than a decision's. An intake takes its case first, through its item; this route has no
 * row to store before the copy, and the API role, which holds no UPDATE on cases, cannot lock a case's row itself. So the
 * post is locked first, and the case's row only by the foreign key of a hold or of the snapshot's own row. A decision
 * takes the case and then its post: the two can wait for each other, and PostgreSQL then makes one give way. Like an
 * intake, the transaction is run again on a deadlock and on a lock timeout, up to three times, and when the last run
 * fails the same way the answer is case_closed: the case would not hold still, and the person tries again.
 */
export async function takeSnapshot(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "social" | "media">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<StaffSnapshotTaken> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await deps.apiDb.transaction((tx) => snapshotIn(deps, tx, row));
    } catch (err) {
      if (!isDeadlock(err) && !isLockNotAvailable(err)) throw err;
      if (attempt >= SNAPSHOT_RETRIES) throw new ModerationError("case_closed");
    }
  }
}

/** One run of the snapshot's transaction: the copy of the case's target, compared with the newest snapshot and stored when it differs. */
async function snapshotIn(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "social" | "media">, tx: DbTx, row: CaseRow): Promise<StaffSnapshotTaken> {
  const caseId = row.id;
  await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${SNAPSHOT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`}::text, true)`);
  // The transaction's start, which the snapshots' trigger stamps and the digest covers.
  const takenAt = await snapshotTime(tx);
  let content: SnapshotContent;
  if (row.targetType === "post") {
    const post = await deps.social.capturePost(tx, row.targetId);
    if (!post) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
    const held = await deps.media.hold(tx, [{ caseId, postId: row.targetId }]);
    content = {
      caseId,
      targetType: "post",
      targetId: row.targetId,
      authorHandle: post.authorHandle,
      postState: post.state,
      postCreatedAt: post.createdAt.toISOString(),
      replyToId: post.replyToId,
      quoteOfId: post.quoteOfId,
      body: post.body,
      media: held.get(row.targetId) ?? [],
      displayName: null,
      bio: null,
      handle: null,
    };
  } else {
    const profile = await deps.social.captureProfile(tx, row.targetId);
    if (!profile) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
    content = {
      caseId,
      targetType: "account",
      targetId: row.targetId,
      authorHandle: profile.handle,
      postState: null,
      postCreatedAt: null,
      replyToId: null,
      quoteOfId: null,
      body: null,
      media: null,
      displayName: profile.displayName,
      bio: profile.bio,
      handle: profile.handle,
    };
  }
  const [newest] = await caseSnapshots(tx, caseId, true);
  if (newest && !newest.withheld && !newest.erased && sameContent(newest, content)) return { id: newest.id, digest: newest.digest };
  return storeSnapshot(tx, takenAt, content);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- a moderator's own finding

/**
 * POST /api/staff/findings: opens a case, or joins the target's open one, on the moderator's own finding under a rule. It
 * runs the transaction every intake runs. A finding needs no key, but it has lasting effects (holds, possibly the urgent
 * lane; citing R2 it freezes what its case reaches and makes the final decision an admin's), so one staff account opens
 * at most the day's limit of them, counted before anything is written, and the home screen lists each account's count.
 *
 * Which targets are live is the one rule of every intake: citing R2, a post in any state and an account also under a
 * handle it has left; under any other rule, only a post its author has not deleted and an account that holds the handle
 * now. A target with nothing live is not_found, and nothing is written: a finding is never stored as answered at once.
 *
 * The target is resolved first, before the day's count is read: a link that names nothing, or another site, is answered
 * as that on any day, and only a finding that could be opened meets the limit.
 */
export async function openFinding(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, request: FindingRequest): Promise<FindingResponse> {
  const { target } = request;
  let named: NamedTarget;
  if (target.kind === "post") named = { type: "post", id: target.id, mediaId: target.mediaId ?? null };
  else if (target.kind === "account") named = { type: "account", handle: target.handle };
  else {
    const parsed = parseLink(deps.config.APP_ORIGIN, target.url);
    named = parsed.type === "post" ? { type: "post", id: parsed.id, mediaId: null } : parsed;
  }
  const suspect = request.ruleId === "R2";
  const found = await liveTarget(deps, named, suspect);
  if (!found) throw new ModerationError("not_found");

  const limits = await dailyLimits(deps.apiDb);
  if ((await findingsOpenedToday(deps.apiDb, session.userId)) >= limits.findings) {
    throw new ModerationError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, secondsToUtcMidnight(deps.now()));
  }

  // A finding alleges no illegality and holds no text of its own: what the moderator writes is a saved text.
  const ground: IntakeGround = {
    kind: "finding",
    channel: "staff",
    reporterId: null,
    findingBy: session.userId,
    contactId: null,
    ruleId: request.ruleId,
    allegesIllegal: false,
    csam: false,
    category: request.category,
    categoryKeyword: null,
    citedLaw: null,
    explanation: null,
    bonaFide: false,
  };
  const live: LiveTarget = named.type === "post" ? { type: "post", id: found.id, position: 1, mediaId: named.mediaId } : { type: "account", id: found.id, position: 1, namedHandle: named.handle };
  const recorded = await recordIntake(deps, { ground, live: [live] });
  const item = recorded.items.find((candidate) => candidate.position === 1);
  if (!item || item.caseId === null) throw new Error("a finding's item was stored without a case");

  // A finding that puts an item into the urgent lane alerts staff as a notice does, after the commit and unwaited for.
  if (recorded.items.some((candidate) => candidate.caseId !== null && candidate.lane === 0)) {
    deps.background.start(async () => {
      await alertUrgentLane(deps);
    });
  }
  return { caseId: item.caseId };
}
```
